# 59 of the 63 tickets orphaned by the 2026-08-03 reconcile incident are STILL parentless

The **code defect** that destroyed these edges is fixed (`88d9-fe42-e50f-4067`, landed
`25ead49f3e`). The **data** was never restored. This ticket tracks that outstanding
restoration backlog, which no open ticket currently owns.

## What happened (re-confirmed independently in this investigation)

Reconcile run **30828160906** (GitHub Actions, `workflow_dispatch`, `MODE: live`,
2026-08-03 15:37:59-15:38:10 UTC) wrote 63 `EDIT` events with
`{"fields": {"parent_id": ""}}`, author `reconciler`, all in one commit
`b8062b10e97b0c891deefbefa87934bb37c66d84` on the `tickets` branch.

**All 63 destroyed a real parent edge. Zero were no-ops.**

The mechanism, cited:
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py:138-139` - outbound
  **OMITS** the parent field whenever the local parent's `ticket_type != "epic"`,
  so Jira is never told about it.
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` `diff_inbound_parent` - inbound
  then read Jira's honest "no parent", classified it `PARENT_NO_PARENT`, and **CLEARED**
  the local edge. Its only guard, `should_propagate_removal`, answers the *outbound*
  question (absent locally -> delete on peer) and structurally cannot answer the inbound
  one. `add_managed_ref` is folded by the **local** parent-set event
  (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:87-90`, `:526-528`), so "managed" never proved Jira
  ever had the parent.
* Omit-vs-clear asymmetry is documented on `39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b`.

**Discriminating evidence (this investigation).** Of tickets holding a parent immediately
before the run: **every one of the 63 lost parents is a `story` (62) or `bug` (1) - not one
`epic`**; 600+ epic-parented children in the same pass were untouched. Story/bug-parented
tickets that survived had **no Jira binding**, so the inbound differ never saw them. The rule
is exact: `cleared <=> bound AND parent is not an epic`. No unexplained residual.

## Why it was never repaired

`8b86-cf7f-ae1c-4955` - 61 of the 63 prior parents are **closed**, and
`rebar edit <child> --parent=<closed parent>` is refused by the `--parent` validation
cascade. `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` (a dedicated `parent` verb with `--force`) is still an
**`idea`**, so no repair route exists today.

## Current state (measured 2026-08-04)

* **59 of 63 still parentless**; 4 restored ad hoc.
* The full child -> lost-parent map is recoverable from the event log and is posted as a
  comment on this ticket.
* The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow is currently `disabled_manually` (last run
  2026-08-04 16:05 UTC), so nothing is re-clearing anything right now.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the recovered child -> lost-parent map is verified against the event log
- [ ] a supported write path exists for re-parenting onto a **closed** parent (depends on
      `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` / `8b86-cf7f-ae1c-4955`)
- [ ] all 59 remaining edges are restored, or each exception is recorded with a reason
- [ ] a post-restore sweep confirms 0 tickets from the incident set remain parentless
- [ ] restoration is done with the reconciler's peer-evidence fix in force, and a
      subsequent reconcile pass is confirmed not to re-clear them
data.title: Restore the 59 tickets still orphaned by the 2026-08-03 reconciler parent-clear incident
